data.body:
Operator decision (2026-08-06): closing without restoring the 59 parent edges.

Measured basis: all 59 orphaned children are ALREADY CLOSED, each with at least one commit in git log matching its full 16-hex ticket id. Nothing in the incident set is unfinished work. The lost edges cost hierarchical provenance only — e.g. story 60ce-29c1-58be-4648 should list 11 children and lists 2 — and cost nothing operationally: ready, next-batch and claim routing all operate on unclosed tickets, and both ends of every broken edge are closed. The layer above is intact (16 of 18 parents retain their own parent edge).

Restoration remains genuinely blocked: rebar edit --parent refuses a closed parent (_resolve_new_parent, src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:503-514), there is no force flag or parent verb, and 5992-f317-e05e-42f7 is still an idea. The only workaround — reopen, re-parent, re-close 18 closed parents — risks stranding them open and costs ~95 reconcile write events to repair a reporting-only defect.

The underlying CODE defect is fixed and closed separately (88d9-fe42-e50f-4067, landed 25ead49f3e), so no defect remains open. 5992 should now be judged on its own merits as a general store-repair capability, not as an urgent unblock for this incident.

Closed via --force-close because the acceptance criteria are written as 'restore all 59 edges' and are therefore literally unmet by design of this decision.
